Excellent! The position after Ndc6+ Ke8 Rxd5 wins material. White has won the knight on d5 and threatens the knight on a5. This is a powerful fork/discovery combination.

**Best move:** Ndc6+

**Main line:** Ndc6+ Ke8 Rxd5 Qxe5 (or Bxc6) Rxd7, winning material

**Motif:** fork (the knight forks king and knight d5, plus discovered attack on d5 from the rook)

**Coaching Note:**
Two Black knights sit on loose squares far from the action. When you have centralized knights and your opponent's king lacks escape squares, look for checks that create multiple threats at once. Ndc6+ forks the king and undefended knight d5—and the rook behind it now attacks that same square. Your opponent cannot defend everything. This pattern (centralized pieces + loose enemy pieces) reveals the winning blow.
